title: Qt: Add legend to TCPStreamDialog
description:
Add a legend to the TCP Stream Dialog. It can be disabled and moved to
various corner and edge positions via the context menu.

Fix #20267

notes.body: changed title from Qt: Add legen to TCPStreamDialog to Qt: Add legend to TCPStreamDialog

added 1 commit
  • b12b962d - Qt: Add legend to TCPStreamDialog
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/21428/diffs?diff_id=1499920372&start_sha=31df47e29d6f96fec759929052e8347fe4f679a4)

Nice addition, there are often a lot f questions about what is what in the tcptrace streamgraph. A few suggestions for improvement:

- make the default position on the top-left (I know a legend is mostly put in the top-right corner) as by default the graph-data will start from bottom-left and will end in the top-right corner of the graph, so placing the legend on the top-right will often be on top of the graph-data.

- Change the graphical representation in the legend a bit (see also my mockup below):
  - Make the segments represented as an I
  - Make both the SACK blocks represented by just a line
  - Add the cumulative ACK line to the Dup ACKs

- invert the use of the legend checkbox, it now is unchecked when the legend is visible and checked when it is hidden. I found this counter intuitive. Another option is to change the text to "Hide legend" 

![image](/uploads/30408fd93f18195480d5af221da177c1/image.png)

Addressed the first and third issue. For the second issue, the Segments not being an I is a bug in QCustomPlot for the default legend icon for QCPErrorBars. To make the others custom, I'll need to write a custom class, so that will take slightly longer.
For the icons, everything is changed except for the Dup ACKs.

The new icons look great. Is a new icon for Dup ACKs in the making, but it takes more time? Or have you chosen not to change it?

On my Debian-13 build system, I see some strange inconsistencies between drag-mode and zoom-mode regarding enabling and disabling the Legend. In drag-mode, after enabling or disabling the legend, the dialog is not changed, until the cursor is moved. In zoom-mode, clicking in the Legend checkbox will result in a first corner of a selection being set instead of the Legend being enabled or disabled.

It would be nice to have a letter assigned to the option to enable and disable the Legend. But the L is part of the old unix cursor keys, the G and D are also taken. The I (if we associate the Legend to an Index) is used for zooming in. It seems the E is available, would it be an idea to use the E as keyboard shortcut?

I plan to change the Dup ACK icon, I just have to make a new subclass for the Dup ACK graph to do it to override the legend icon.

I'll investigate the other issues.
The legend should update now. The issue with zoom-mode starting a zoom selection appears to happen on the context menu for any item (but does not happen with the IO Graph.) I'll have to look into it.
Ah, I need to do the same fix for TCPStreamDialog that I did for IO Graph in 41b7489572f2cb862a86398b45b113f7d9705153
Dup ACK icon changed.

The icons look great now! One nitpicking suggestion, can the Dup ACK icon be moved under the ACK icon? That way the order of the legend feels more logical (data related, ACK related, Window size related).

Also, the irregularities regarding enabling/disabling are now mostly gone. Except for when in zoom mode, the enabling/disabling works correct but it does still also start a zoom selection.

The zoom selection issue is long standing and fixed by !21463 separately.

On Windows, because Windows has a longstanding platform habit of "selecting or lassoing items in File Explorer with the right mouse button and then popping up a context menu," Qt pops up a context menu on RightButton *release*. On other platforms, the context menu pops up when RightButton is *pressed*. For the former, it can sometimes be ok to start a zoom window when RightButton clicking, but it's really broken with the latter.
Re: moving the icon, sure, that's easy, we just create and add the graphs in the appropriate order. Done.
